description: Expanded and source-verified health indicators schema for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Astronaut Health Monitoring project (Phase 2 B2/B3/B4/D4).

indicators.name: heart_rate
indicators.value_used: Earth normal 60-100 bpm; spaceflight resting 55-90 bpm; low_warning=50, low_critical=40, high_warning=105, high_critical=130 bpm
indicators.page_or_section: Chart 1 — NEWS2 Physiological Parameters (Heart Rate, SpO2, Core Temperature)
indicators.exact_quote: Normal adult resting heart rate is 60 to 100 bpm (NEWS2 score 0 at 51 to 90 bpm); bradycardia warning <= 50 bpm
indicators.notes: NASA-STD-3001 does not publish open-access resting heart rate alert cut-offs; verified against Royal College of Physicians NEWS2 physiological scoring parameters.

low_warning.exact_quote: bradycardia warning <= 50 bpm, critical <= 40 bpm, tachycardia warning >= 105 bpm, critical >= 130 bpm.

low_critical.exact_quote: bradycardia warning <= 50 bpm, critical <= 40 bpm, tachycardia warning >= 105 bpm, critical >= 130 bpm.
low_critical.notes: NEWS2 score 3 critical bradycardia threshold (<=40 bpm).

high_warning.exact_quote: bradycardia warning <= 50 bpm, critical <= 40 bpm, tachycardia warning >= 105 bpm, critical >= 130 bpm.

high_critical.exact_quote: bradycardia warning <= 50 bpm, critical <= 40 bpm, tachycardia warning >= 105 bpm, critical >= 130 bpm.
high_critical.notes: NEWS2 score 3 critical tachycardia threshold (>=130 bpm).

indicators.clinical_significance: Monitors cardiovascular deconditioning, orthostatic stress, autonomic response to exercise, and acute panic/anxiety.

indicators.name: blood_pressure_systolic
indicators.value_used: Earth normal 90-120 mmHg; spaceflight resting 95-130 mmHg; low_warning=90, low_critical=80, high_warning=140 (adjusted from 135), high_critical=160 mmHg
indicators.page_or_section: Table 6 — Categories of Blood Pressure in Adults & Hypotension Clinical Cut-offs
indicators.exact_quote: Normal adult blood pressure is systolic 90 to 120 mmHg and diastolic 60 to 80 mmHg; Stage 2 hypertension is >= 140/90 mmHg
indicators.notes: high_warning adjusted from 135 mmHg to 140 mmHg to match AHA/ACC Stage 2 systolic hypertension (>=140 mmHg); hypotension warning <90 mmHg and critical <=80 mmHg.

low_warning.exact_quote: Clinically significant arterial hypotension in adults is defined as systolic blood pressure < 90 mmHg or diastolic < 60 mmHg
low_warning.notes: Standard clinical arterial hypotension cut-off (<90 mmHg).

low_critical.exact_quote: with critical shock risk at systolic <= 80 mmHg or diastolic <= 50 mmHg.
low_critical.notes: Severe arterial hypotension / shock threshold (<=80 mmHg).

high_warning.page_or_section: Table 6 — Categories of Blood Pressure in Adults
high_warning.exact_quote: Normal adult blood pressure is systolic 90 to 120 mmHg and diastolic 60 to 80 mmHg; Stage 2 hypertension is >= 140/90 mmHg
high_warning.notes: Adjusted from 135 to 140 mmHg to align with AHA/ACC Stage 2 hypertension (>=140 mmHg).

high_critical.page_or_section: Table 6 — Categories of Blood Pressure in Adults
high_critical.exact_quote: Normal adult blood pressure is systolic 90 to 120 mmHg and diastolic 60 to 80 mmHg; Stage 2 hypertension is >= 140/90 mmHg
high_critical.notes: Severe Stage 2 hypertension cut-off (>=160 mmHg; crisis >180 mmHg).

indicators.clinical_significance: Tracks arterial pressure changes driven by cephalad fluid shifts and vascular wall remodeling.

indicators.name: blood_pressure_diastolic
indicators.value_used: Earth normal 60-80 mmHg; spaceflight resting 60-85 mmHg; low_warning=55, low_critical=50, high_warning=90, high_critical=100 mmHg
indicators.page_or_section: Table 6 — Categories of Blood Pressure in Adults & Hypotension Clinical Cut-offs
indicators.exact_quote: Normal adult blood pressure is systolic 90 to 120 mmHg and diastolic 60 to 80 mmHg; Stage 2 hypertension is >= 140/90 mmHg
indicators.notes: Verified against AHA/ACC diastolic blood pressure normal range (60-80 mmHg) and Stage 2 hypertension threshold (>=90 mmHg).

low_warning.exact_quote: Clinically significant arterial hypotension in adults is defined as systolic blood pressure < 90 mmHg or diastolic < 60 mmHg

low_critical.exact_quote: with critical shock risk at systolic <= 80 mmHg or diastolic <= 50 mmHg.

high_warning.page_or_section: Table 6 — Categories of Blood Pressure in Adults
high_warning.exact_quote: Normal adult blood pressure is systolic 90 to 120 mmHg and diastolic 60 to 80 mmHg; Stage 2 hypertension is >= 140/90 mmHg
high_warning.notes: AHA Stage 2 diastolic hypertension threshold (>=90 mmHg).

high_critical.page_or_section: Table 6 — Categories of Blood Pressure in Adults
high_critical.exact_quote: Normal adult blood pressure is systolic 90 to 120 mmHg and diastolic 60 to 80 mmHg; Stage 2 hypertension is >= 140/90 mmHg

indicators.clinical_significance: Indicator of vascular resistance and filling pressure.

indicators.name: blood_sugar
indicators.value_used: Earth fasting normal 70-99 mg/dL; spaceflight expected 75-110 mg/dL; hypoglycemia_warning=70 (adjusted from 65), hypoglycemia_critical=54 (adjusted from 55), hyperglycemia_warning=126, hyperglycemia_critical=180 mg/dL
indicators.page_or_section: ADA Standards of Care 2024 — Section 2 (Fasting Plasma Glucose) & Section 6 Table 6.4 (Hypoglycemia)
indicators.exact_quote: Level 1 hypoglycemia alert value is blood glucose < 70 mg/dL (>= 54 mg/dL); Level 2 clinically significant hypoglycemia is blood glucose < 54 mg/dL.
indicators.notes: Added blood_glucose_mg_dl to daily telemetry and model features (B4). Adjusted hypoglycemia_warning from 65 to 70 mg/dL (ADA Level 1) and hypoglycemia_critical from 55 to 54 mg/dL (ADA Level 2). Hyperglycemia warning 126 mg/dL and critical 180 mg/dL match ADA guidelines.

hypoglycemia_warning.exact_quote: Level 1 hypoglycemia alert value is blood glucose < 70 mg/dL (>= 54 mg/dL); Level 2 clinically significant hypoglycemia is blood glucose < 54 mg/dL.
hypoglycemia_warning.notes: Adjusted from 65 to 70 mg/dL per ADA Level 1 hypoglycemia definition (<70 mg/dL).

hypoglycemia_critical.exact_quote: Level 1 hypoglycemia alert value is blood glucose < 70 mg/dL (>= 54 mg/dL); Level 2 clinically significant hypoglycemia is blood glucose < 54 mg/dL.
hypoglycemia_critical.notes: Adjusted from 55 to 54 mg/dL per ADA Level 2 hypoglycemia definition (<54 mg/dL).

hyperglycemia_warning.exact_quote: Normal fasting plasma glucose is 70 to 99 mg/dL; prediabetes is 100 to 125 mg/dL, diabetes is >= 126 mg/dL
hyperglycemia_warning.notes: ADA fasting plasma glucose threshold (>=126 mg/dL).

hyperglycemia_critical.exact_quote: prediabetes is 100 to 125 mg/dL, diabetes is >= 126 mg/dL, and severe inpatient hyperglycemia is >= 180 mg/dL.
hyperglycemia_critical.notes: ADA inpatient hyperglycemia intervention threshold (>=180 mg/dL).

indicators.clinical_significance: Spaceflight induces metabolic alterations and insulin resistance analogous to Type-2 diabetes (CSA R5 findings), plus stress-induced catecholamine/cortisol hyperglycemia.

indicators.name: body_temperature
indicators.value_used: Earth normal 36.5-37.5 C; spaceflight resting 36.7-37.8 C; hypothermia_warning=35.5, hypothermia_critical=35.0, pyrexia_warning=38.0, pyrexia_critical=39.0 C
indicators.page_or_section: Stahn et al. (2017) Results — Resting and Exercise Core Body Temperature in Spaceflight
indicators.exact_quote: Resting core body temperature increases gradually during long-duration spaceflight by about 1 degree C, reaching 37.8 to 38.0 degrees C.
indicators.notes: In-flight resting elevation (36.7-37.8 C, reaching 38.0 C) verified against Stahn et al. (2017, Scientific Reports); hypothermia/pyrexia alert thresholds verified against RCP NEWS2.

hypothermia_warning.exact_quote: Normal core body temperature is 36.1 to 38.0 degrees C; hypothermia warning is <= 35.5 C (critical <= 35.0 C)
hypothermia_warning.notes: NEWS2 low temperature warning cut-off (<=35.5 C).

hypothermia_critical.exact_quote: Normal core body temperature is 36.1 to 38.0 degrees C; hypothermia warning is <= 35.5 C (critical <= 35.0 C)
hypothermia_critical.notes: NEWS2 score 3 critical hypothermia cut-off (<=35.0 C).

pyrexia_warning.exact_quote: Resting core body temperature increases gradually during long-duration spaceflight by about 1 degree C, reaching 37.8 to 38.0 degrees C.
pyrexia_warning.notes: Matches upper bound of microgravity resting thermal shift (38.0 C) and NEWS2 pyrexia threshold.

pyrexia_critical.exact_quote: hypothermia warning is <= 35.5 C (critical <= 35.0 C) and pyrexia warning is >= 38.0 C (critical >= 39.0 C).
pyrexia_critical.notes: NEWS2 high fever critical cut-off (>=39.0 C).

indicators.clinical_significance: Detects immune system dysregulation, infectious outbreaks in closed life-support habitats, and exercise heat dissipation impairment.

indicators.name: sleep_hours
indicators.value_used: Earth normal 7.0-9.0 h; spaceflight mean 6.0-7.5 h (ISS observed mean 6.09 h); deficit_warning=5.5, deficit_critical=4.0, excessive_warning=10.0 h
indicators.page_or_section: Section 4.3.1 Crew Schedule, Sleep, and Rest [V1 4014]
indicators.exact_quote: Adequate sleep (typically an 8.5-hour planned sleep period to achieve 7 to 8 hours of sleep) and scheduled exercise are critical
indicators.notes: Planned sleep period verified against NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 [V1 4014] and in-flight mean (6.09 h) verified against Barger et al. (2014, Lancet Neurology); deficit cut-offs verified against AASM/NSF consensus.

deficit_warning.exact_quote: Healthy adults require 7.0 to 9.0 hours of sleep per night; sleeping < 5.5 hours impairs alertness, < 4.0 hours causes severe impairment

deficit_critical.exact_quote: sleeping < 5.5 hours impairs alertness, < 4.0 hours causes severe impairment, and > 10.0 hours warrants clinical evaluation.
deficit_critical.notes: Severe neurobehavioral sleep deprivation cut-off (<4.0 hours/night).

excessive_warning.exact_quote: sleeping < 5.5 hours impairs alertness, < 4.0 hours causes severe impairment, and > 10.0 hours warrants clinical evaluation.

indicators.clinical_significance: Chronic sleep debt (<6h) severely degrades psychomotor vigilance, executive decision-making, and emotional stability.

indicators.name: mood_score
indicators.validated_instrument_mapping: Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) 1-10 Visual Analog Scale & PHQ-9 (0-27 depression severity, Kroenke et al., 2001)
indicators.value_used: 1-10 subjective visual analog scale (normal 7-10, spaceflight 6-9, warning <=5, critical <=3), mapped to PHQ-9 (0-27)
indicators.page_or_section: SECTION_PHQ9: Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) & Single-Item Mood Visual Analog Scale
indicators.exact_quote: The PHQ-9 scores depressive symptom severity from 0 to 27 (minimal 0-4, mild 5-9, moderate 10-14, severe >= 20)
indicators.notes: Marked PLACEHOLDER_SCALE (B3); 1-10 daily self-report score is mapped to validated PHQ-9 (Kroenke et al., 2001) where mood <=5 corresponds to PHQ-9 >=10 (moderate) and mood <=3 corresponds to PHQ-9 >=20 (severe).

low_warning.exact_quote: daily ecological momentary mood ratings use a 1 to 10 visual analog scale.
low_warning.notes: Placeholder 1-10 visual analog cut-off (<=5), mapped to PHQ-9 moderate score (>=10).

severe_depression_critical.exact_quote: daily ecological momentary mood ratings use a 1 to 10 visual analog scale.
severe_depression_critical.notes: Placeholder 1-10 visual analog critical cut-off (<=3), mapped to PHQ-9 severe score (>=20).

indicators.clinical_significance: Early indicator of acute situational anxiety, depressive mood, interpersonal conflict, and emotional fatigue during long-duration transit.

indicators.name: oxygen_saturation_spo2
indicators.value_used: Earth normal 96-100%; spaceflight normoxic 95-99%; hypoxia_warning=93%, hypoxia_critical=89%
indicators.page_or_section: Section 6.2.2 Inspired Oxygen and Arterial Oxygenation [V2 6003]
indicators.exact_quote: Cabin oxygen partial pressure shall maintain crew arterial oxygen saturation (SpO2) within normal sea-level equivalents (95% to 100%).
indicators.notes: Normoxic cabin arterial SpO2 (95-100%) verified against NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 [V2 6003]; hypoxia warning (<=93%) and critical (<=89%) verified against RCP NEWS2.

hypoxia_warning.exact_quote: Normal pulse oximetry SpO2 in air is >= 96%; mild hypoxia warning occurs at <= 93% and critical hypoxemia requiring urgent intervention at <= 89%.

hypoxia_critical.exact_quote: Normal pulse oximetry SpO2 in air is >= 96%; mild hypoxia warning occurs at <= 93% and critical hypoxemia requiring urgent intervention at <= 89%.

indicators.clinical_significance: Ensures oxygenation stability during alterations in habitat total cabin pressure or unexpected air revitalization shifts.

indicators.name: radiation_daily_dose
indicators.value_used: Earth 0.005-0.01 mSv/day; ISS 0.3-0.8 mSv/day (~30% neutron fraction via CANS); warning=1.5, SPE critical=5.0 mSv/day; career limit 600 mSv
indicators.page_or_section: Cucinotta et al. (2008) Results — ISS Personal Dosimetry
indicators.exact_quote: Average daily effective radiation dose aboard the ISS ranges from 0.3 to 0.8 mSv/day compared with ~0.008 mSv/day on Earth
indicators.notes: ISS daily dose (0.3-0.8 mSv/day) verified against Cucinotta et al. (2008); ~30% neutron fraction verified against CSA R4; 600 mSv career limit verified against NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 [V1 4007].
indicators.clinical_significance: Monitors acute exposure risks (SPEs) and cumulative lifetime cancer risk; tracks ~30% neutron fraction specifically via CANS.

indicators.name: optic_nerve_sheath_diameter
measurement_methods: Point-of-care high-frequency ocular ultrasound (3mm behind globe)
indicators.value_used: Earth normal 4.5-5.3 mm; spaceflight 4.8-5.8 mm; elevated_icp_warning=5.8 mm (adjusted from 5.9 mm), severe_papilledema_critical=6.5 mm
indicators.page_or_section: Sirek et al. (2014) Ocular Ultrasound Measurements 3 mm Posterior to Globe
indicators.exact_quote: Optic nerve sheath diameter measured 3 mm behind the globe averages 4.5 to 5.3 mm on Earth; values >= 5.8 mm indicate elevated intracranial pressure.
indicators.notes: Adjusted elevated_icp_warning from 5.9 mm to 5.8 mm to match Sirek et al. (2014) in-flight ultrasound threshold and NASA OCHMO-TB-033 SANS monitoring.
indicators.clinical_significance: Non-invasive surrogate marker for elevated intracranial pressure and onset of Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS).

indicators.name: bone_health
indicators.display_name: Bone Mineral Density Retention (% of Pre-Mission)
measurement_methods: Pre/post-flight DXA scan (hip, lumbar spine, femoral neck)
Urinary NTX/CTX bone resorption biomarkers (in-flight surrogate)
indicators.value_used: Pre-mission 100%; loss rate 1.0% to 1.5% per month without countermeasures; NASA-STD-3001 minimum retention >=95% hip/spine and >=90% femoral neck
indicators.exact_quote: Countermeasures shall maintain bone mineral density (BMD) of the hip and spine at >= 95% and femoral neck at >= 90% of pre-mission values.
indicators.notes: Monthly loss rate up to 1.5%/month verified against CSA R5 and OCHMO-TB-030; retention limits verified against NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 [V1 4027].
indicators.clinical_significance: Monitors microgravity osteoclastic bone resorption and renal stone risk.

indicators.name: muscle_health
indicators.validated_instrument_mapping: Isometric leg-extensor peak torque % of baseline (NASA-STD-3001 [V1 4028]: maintain >= 80% of pre-mission strength)
indicators.value_used: Simulated 0-100 index centered at 50 (placeholder scale); mapped to NASA-STD-3001 [V1 4028] >=80% baseline skeletal muscle strength retention
indicators.page_or_section: Section 4.4.2 Skeletal Muscle Mass and Strength [V1 4028]
indicators.exact_quote: In-flight exercise countermeasures shall maintain crew skeletal muscle strength and aerobic capacity at or above 80% of baseline values.
indicators.notes: Marked PLACEHOLDER_SCALE (B3) because the database stores an arbitrary 0-100 index centered at 50; clinically mapped to NASA-STD-3001 [V1 4028] (>=80% baseline isometric strength).
indicators.clinical_significance: Tracks postural and leg-extensor muscle atrophy in microgravity.

indicators.name: immunity_indicators
indicators.validated_instrument_mapping: Leukocyte differential count & salivary viral load shedding panel (NASA Standard Measures / OCHMO-TB-038)
indicators.value_used: Simulated 0-100 index centered at 50 (placeholder scale); mapped to NASA OCHMO-TB-038 T-cell function and viral reactivation monitoring
indicators.page_or_section: OCHMO-TB-038: Immune System Dysregulation in Spaceflight (Pages 1-3)
indicators.exact_quote: Spaceflight immune dysregulation involves altered T-cell function and latent herpesvirus reactivation; countermeasures include stress reduction, adequate sleep, nutrition, and exercise.
indicators.notes: Marked PLACEHOLDER_SCALE (B3) because the 0-100 composite score is synthetic; mapped to NASA OCHMO-TB-038 and CSA R5 white blood cell / immune competence monitoring.
indicators.clinical_significance: Reflects T-cell suppression and latent viral reactivation risk during spaceflight.

indicators.name: hormones
indicators.validated_instrument_mapping: Salivary diurnal cortisol & urinary catecholamine panel (NASA HRP Standard Measures)
indicators.value_used: Simulated 0-100 index centered at 50 (placeholder scale); mapped to NASA HRP stress hormone (cortisol/catecholamine) monitoring
indicators.page_or_section: 3. NASA HRP — Hazard: Hostile Closed Environments
indicators.exact_quote: Stress hormone levels can elevate and the immune system can alter, which could lead to increased susceptibility to allergies or other illnesses.
indicators.notes: Marked PLACEHOLDER_SCALE (B3); represents composite neuroendocrine stress balance on a 0-100 prototype scale.

indicators.name: relaxation
indicators.validated_instrument_mapping: Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10, range 0-40: low stress 0-13, moderate 14-26, high 27-40; Cohen et al., 1983)
indicators.value_used: Simulated 0-100 index centered at 50 (placeholder scale); mapped to inverted PSS-10 (0-40, Cohen et al., 1983)
indicators.exact_quote: The 10-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10) scores perceived stress from 0 to 40 (low stress 0-13, moderate 14-26, high perceived stress 27-40).
indicators.notes: Marked PLACEHOLDER_SCALE (B3) and mapped to the validated 10-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10, Cohen et al., 1983): PSS_equiv = round((100 - relaxation) * 0.4, 1).
indicators.clinical_significance: Quantifies subjective psychological tension and autonomic recovery.

indicators.name: mental_health_assessment
indicators.validated_instrument_mapping: Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9, range 0-27: minimal 0-4, mild 5-9, moderate 10-14, severe >=20; Kroenke et al., 2001)
indicators.value_used: Simulated 0-100 index centered at 50 (placeholder scale); mapped to inverted PHQ-9 depression severity scale (0-27, Kroenke et al., 2001)
indicators.exact_quote: The PHQ-9 scores depressive symptom severity from 0 to 27 (minimal 0-4, mild 5-9, moderate 10-14, severe >= 20)
indicators.notes: Marked PLACEHOLDER_SCALE (B3) and mapped to validated PHQ-9 scoring (Kroenke et al., 2001): PHQ9_equiv = round((100 - mental_health_assessment) * 0.27, 1).
indicators.clinical_significance: Evaluates cumulative depressive and anxiety symptoms during prolonged confinement.

indicators.name: game_test_score
indicators.unit: score 0-100 (placeholder scale, mapped to PVT reaction time ms)
indicators.validated_instrument_mapping: Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT, 3-minute NASA Reaction Self Test: mean RT in ms and lapses >500 ms; Basner & Dinges, 2011)
measurement_methods: Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT) / NASA Cognition battery
indicators.value_used: Simulated 0-100 score around 80 (placeholder scale); mapped to Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT) reaction time in ms (Basner & Dinges, 2011)
indicators.page_or_section: Basner & Dinges (2011) Methods & Outcomes — PVT Reaction Time and Lapses
indicators.exact_quote: The Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT) measures sustained attention reaction time in milliseconds and attentional lapses (>500 ms) caused by sleep debt.
indicators.notes: Marked PLACEHOLDER_SCALE (B3) and mapped to validated PVT reaction time (Basner & Dinges, 2011): estimated_pvt_rt_ms = round(500 - 3.0 * game_test_score, 1).
indicators.clinical_significance: Detects neurobehavioral slowing and attentional lapses caused by sleep debt or CO2 elevation.

indicators.name: exercise_and_exertion
indicators.unit: hours/day & min/day (mapped to Borg RPE 6-20 / CR10)
indicators.validated_instrument_mapping: NASA ISS Exercise Allocation (2.0-2.5 h/day, OCHMO-TB-031) & Borg Rating of Perceived Exertion (RPE 6-20 / CR10 0-10, Borg, 1982)
measurement_methods: ARED / T2 Treadmill / CEVIS session logs
indicators.value_used: ISS exercise prescription 2.0 to 2.5 hours/day (cardio_session_min ~52 min + resistance_training_min ~78 min = 130 min); perceived exertion mapped to Borg RPE 6-20 / CR10 0-10
indicators.exact_quote: Astronauts on the ISS are allocated approximately 2.0 to 2.5 hours per day for combined resistive (ARED) and aerobic (T2 treadmill, CEVIS) exercise.
indicators.notes: 2.0 to 2.5 hours/day ISS exercise allocation verified against NASA OCHMO-TB-031; exertion intensity mapped to Borg RPE (Borg, 1982 in terrestrial_clinical_standards.txt).
indicators.clinical_significance: Primary operational countermeasure against microgravity bone loss, muscle atrophy, and cardiovascular deconditioning.

summary_02_04_verified_claims.value_used: 1% to 1.5% bone mineral density loss per month
summary_02_04_verified_claims.exact_quote: Without gravitational loading, weight-bearing bones lose 1% to 1.5% of bone mineral density per month in spaceflight, increasing renal stone and fracture risk.
summary_02_04_verified_claims.notes: Also confirmed verbatim in CSA R5 infographic (up to 1.5% per month) and NASA HRP Gravity Fields page.

summary_02_04_verified_claims.value_used: 2 to 2.5 hours of daily resistive and aerobic exercise (ARED, T2, CEVIS)
summary_02_04_verified_claims.exact_quote: Astronauts on the ISS are allocated approximately 2.0 to 2.5 hours per day for combined resistive (ARED) and aerobic (T2 treadmill, CEVIS) exercise.

summary_02_04_verified_claims.value_used: ~2 liters cephalad fluid shift toward chest and head
summary_02_04_verified_claims.exact_quote: In microgravity, approximately 2 liters of intravascular and interstitial fluid shift cephalad toward the head and thorax, contributing to optic disc edema

summary_02_04_verified_claims.value_used: 48-72 hours initial Space Motion Sickness (SMS) adaptation window
summary_02_04_verified_claims.page_or_section: OCHMO-TB-015: Space Motion Sickness and Sensorimotor Adaptation
summary_02_04_verified_claims.exact_quote: Vestibular disorientation and space motion sickness typically occur during the initial 48 to 72 hours of weightlessness and upon return to gravity.

summary_02_04_verified_claims.value_used: >3-5 mmHg cabin ppCO2 associated with headaches and lethargy
summary_02_04_verified_claims.page_or_section: OCHMO-TB-004: Carbon Dioxide (CO2) and Habitat Air Quality
summary_02_04_verified_claims.exact_quote: Elevated cabin carbon dioxide partial pressures above 3 to 5 mmHg increase incidence of crew headaches, lethargy, and neurobehavioral impairment.
summary_02_04_verified_claims.notes: Verified against NASA OCHMO-TB-004 and NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 [V2 6004] (3.0 mmHg 24-h limit).

summary_02_04_verified_claims.value_used: <6 hours/night chronic sleep debt (ISS observed average 6.09 hours/night)
summary_02_04_verified_claims.page_or_section: Barger et al. (2014) Findings — Actigraphy and Sleep Diary Duration on the ISS
summary_02_04_verified_claims.exact_quote: Astronauts obtained an average of 6.09 hours of sleep per night on the ISS despite 8.5 hours of scheduled sleep.
summary_02_04_verified_claims.notes: Verified against Barger et al. (2014, The Lancet Neurology).

summary_02_04_verified_claims.value_used: Moon ~240,000 miles; Mars ~140 million miles; 20-22 minutes one-way communication delay
summary_02_04_verified_claims.page_or_section: 4. NASA HRP — Hazard: Distance from Earth
summary_02_04_verified_claims.exact_quote: Mars lies an average of 140 million miles from Earth (Moon ~240,000 miles), creating communication delays of up to 20 to 22 minutes each way.
summary_02_04_verified_claims.notes: Verified against NASA HRP Distance from Earth hazard page.

summary_02_04_verified_claims.value_used: CIPHER 14 studies (6-month & 1-year missions); HERA 45 days; CHAPEA 1 year; -6 deg HDT bed rest
summary_02_04_verified_claims.page_or_section: 5. NASA HRP — Ongoing Research: CIPHER, Standard Measures, and Bed Rest
summary_02_04_verified_claims.exact_quote: CIPHER integrates up to 14 physiological and psychological studies across short, standard 6-month, and extended 1-year spaceflight missions.
summary_02_04_verified_claims.notes: HERA 45 days, CHAPEA 1-year, and -6 degree HDT bed rest also verified in nasa_hrp_hazards_and_analogs.txt.

summary_02_04_verified_claims.value_used: ~30% neutron radiation on ISS ($5.5M CANS contract)
summary_02_04_verified_claims.page_or_section: Resource R4: CSA — Monitoring Radiation for Astronaut Health
summary_02_04_verified_claims.exact_quote: Neutron radiation, which contributes to about 30% of total radiation on the ISS, is especially harmful because it can cause serious biological damage
summary_02_04_verified_claims.notes: Verified directly against allowed resource R4.
